title: Grateful Dead Live at Hofheinz Pavilion on 1972-11-18
lineage: Dat (Tascam DA-20) -> Tascam SS-R05 -> Adobe Audition v3.0 ->Samplitude Professional v11.2.1 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 11/18/1972 Houston show with a smoking Playing in the Band and solid soundboard source that’s good overall despite minor speed/pitch quirks
ai_review.review: The performance is hailed as one of the band’s peak ’72 shows – Phil “bombs” on bass, Jerry’s wah‑infused tone shines, and the second set (Deal → Playing in the Band → Uncle John’s) is described as a relentless, joyous groove. The recording is a soundboard (SBD) that most listeners find clear and balanced, though a few note slight wow and pitch‑shift issues on certain tracks.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly enthusiastic comments about the music (standout jams, high energy) combined with generally favorable notes on the soundboard quality (clear but with minor speed/pitch quirks) yield a strong rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear SBD mix, but some listeners report slight wow in early tracks and pitch‑correction needs on Jack Straw/He's Gone; occasional cuts in Sugar Magnolia.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Second set is the highlight, building from a mellow Bertha into a rapturous Greatest Story and then a marathon Playing In The Band that drives the night’s momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His wah‑infused tone and big grin are repeatedly praised; his guitar work is called “incredible” and “locked in”.
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as an "absolute animal" who "bombs" on bass, providing the driving force throughout the jam.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocal phrasing noted as locked perfectly with Bill’s drumming; praised for his melodic contributions.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's tasteful fills are highlighted during the improvisational sections.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming is called tight and supportive, helping keep the groove solid.
